title: Question tags (…, isn't it? …, don't you?)
en:
A question tag is a short question at the end of a sentence. We use it to check information or to invite the other person to agree.

Positive sentence → negative tag: It's cold, isn't it? You work in finance, don't you?

Negative sentence → positive tag: You aren't busy, are you? He didn't call, did he?

Use the same auxiliary (am/is/are, do/does/did, have, can, will…). No auxiliary in the sentence → do / does / did. Special: I'm late, aren't I? Let's start, shall we?
ru: Хвостик-вопрос: утверждение → отрицательный хвост (It's cold, isn't it?), отрицание → положительный (You aren't busy, are you?). Тот же вспомогательный глагол; если его нет — do/does/did. Исключения: I'm…, aren't I? Let's…, shall we?

boss.situation: You are meeting a new colleague. Check 5 facts about them with question tags (both positive and negative sentences).
samples: You joined the company last month, didn't you?
You haven't worked in audit before, have you?
You can speak Kazakh, can't you?
You don't have a meeting now, do you?

qs.exp: No auxiliary → do; positive → don't you.

qs.q: “You can swim, can you?” is correct.
Put the words in the correct order.
qs.a: you are not busy are you

qs.q: Put the words in the correct order.
qs.a: he did not call did he

qs.q: Put the words in the correct order.
qs.a: we will not be late will we

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “You're the new auditor, isn't it?”
a: You're the new auditor, aren't you?
You are the new auditor, aren't you?
